title: API Security Guidelines
content:
API Security Guidelines v2.0

The API Security Guidelines are owned by the Security Team and enforced by the Engineering Team.

Authentication Requirements:
- All external APIs must use OAuth 2.0 with PKCE flow
- Internal service-to-service communication uses mutual TLS (mTLS)
- API keys must be rotated every 90 days
- No API should accept unauthenticated requests in production

Rate Limiting:
- Public APIs: 100 requests per minute per client
- Internal APIs: 1000 requests per minute per service
- Admin APIs: 50 requests per minute per user

Data Protection:
- All APIs must encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.3
- Personally identifiable information (PII) must be encrypted at rest
- API responses must never expose stack traces or internal error messages
- The Data Retention Policy applies to all data cached by API services

Logging and Monitoring:
- All API calls must be logged with timestamp, client ID, and response code
- Failed authentication attempts must trigger alerts to the Security Team
- API latency above 500ms triggers PagerDuty alerts for SEV2 classification

The Security Team conducts quarterly API penetration testing. All critical findings must be remediated within 7 days.

The Engineering Team must conduct code review for all API changes. Security-sensitive changes require additional review by the Security Team.
